newsitem.title: USA: Calif. approves MCI, Sprint local plans.
newsitem.headline: Calif. approves MCI, Sprint local plans.

text.p: California's utility regulators Thursday permitted MCI Communications Corp and Sprint Corp to enter California's local telephone market by approving interconnect deals they reached with local providers.

In Interconnect agreements reached with Pacific Telesis Group, MCI and Sprint each get a 17 percent discount off Pacific Bell's resale prices. Pacific Bell is the California telephone operating unit of Pacific Telesis.
In an interconnect agreement with GTE Corp's GTE California unit, MCI gets a 12 percent discount for business services and seven percent for residentail services.
The California Public Utility Commission approved all these agreements in a session Thursday. An interconnect agreement between GTE and Sprint has not been finalized.

"These, along with the ones approved previously for AT&T Communications of Calfornia, pave the way for the three major long distance telecommunications companies to begin competing with Pacific Bell, GTE California Inc and each other to offer local phone service," the commission said in a statement.
"The commission expects local service competition to produce the same benefits toll serve competition has including lower rates and more options for consumers," it said.

AT&T Corp, through earlier approved interconnect agreements, also gets a 17-percent discount off the resale prices of Pacific Bell and a 12-percent discount from GTE's business service prices and seven percent from GTE's residential price.
The commission said it was up to the companies as to when they want to start offering service.
Neither MCI, Sprint nor Pacific Bell could be reached immediately for comment.
